title: Nonstationary bandits: known variance budget and unknown variation budget.
summary: A fixed sequence of bounded reward distributions may vary over time, and the learner observes only the selected arm's reward. One algorithm must adapt to every undisclosed budget; performance is evaluated using the actual environment's variance and mean variation. Different levels of budget knowledge cannot be interchanged.

model.instance: There are $K\ge2$ arms. The reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ are fixed before interaction, supported on $[0,1]$, and sampled independently across rounds. Denote means by $\mu_{t,i}=\mathbb E X_{t,i}$ and their vector by $\mu_t$. $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{env}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\max_{1\le i\le K}\operatorname{Var}(X_{t,i})\le\frac T4.$$ The quantity $Q_{\mathrm{env}}$ sums the largest arm variance in each round; it is neither the variance sum along the chosen arms nor the sum over all arms.

operations.query_signature: Choose arm $I_t$ and observe one reward $X_{t,I_t}$. Noise may be heteroscedastic or zero; reward laws may vary over time even when means are constant. Inputs $K,T$ and variance-budget bound $Q$ satisfying $Q_{\mathrm{env}}\le Q$ are public. Armwise variances, means, change locations, and drift budget $V$ are hidden. Policies must be causal, cannot use undisclosed budgets, and must work simultaneously over all such unknown-budget classes. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\begin{aligned}[c]\mathcal{R}_T^*&\ge c\,\Xi(K,T;Q,V),\\ \Xi(K,T;Q,V)&=\min\left\{T,\ K+\sqrt{KQ}+(KQVT)^{1/3}\right.\\ &\hspace{7em}\left.+\sqrt{KT}\min\{V,\sqrt V\}\right\}.\end{aligned}$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: The source statements and budget conventions have been checked. This profile uses only the explicitly compatible portions of the linked atomic bounds. Lower bounds may transfer by restricting public information; upper bounds with two known budgets do not transfer automatically when less information is available. Full proofs have not been independently reconstructed line by line; this does not alter the recorded status of the source theorems.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\widetilde{O}\!\left(\min\{T,\sqrt{KT}+(KV_\mu)^{1/3}T^{2/3}\}\right)$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Insert UCB1 coefficients $c_1\asymp\sqrt K$ and $c_2\asymp K$ into MASTER Theorem 2. Choose failure probability $T^{-2}$ and use $0\le R_T\le T$ for the expectation bound; cap endpoints by $T$. The same policy handles all realized variations $V_\mu$ without taking variation as input.
